summary: Setup and refresh now judge every model a role is pinned to, the project's `tier_models` included, against the host's own model list, read from the binary that runs the session without a model request, and fall back to the session's model with a visible warning when the list does not hold one; both host contracts state this one strategy in the same words. Each host package ships `scripts/host_models.py` over a shared core, `host_listing.py`: it judges a model `available` when the list holds it and reflects the signed-in account, `unavailable` when the list does not hold it, since that binary cannot run it, and `unverified` when no list could be read or the list reflects no account. Every probe runs within one time limit and stops every process it started when the limit passes, and any failure gives `unverified`, never an error that stops setup. On Claude Code the binary is `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH` or the executable of `CLAUDE_PID`, else `claude` on PATH when its version meets the highest `min_cli_version` of the catalog models the tiers run, which `templates/tier-map.json` now ships per model; the list is the `models` of its reply to one `initialize` control request, sent with every hook off, no user message and no MCP server loaded (`--strict-mcp-config`), so it starts none of the project's `.mcp.json` servers, which an interactive session asks the user to approve first, and no user or plugin server, and it reflects the account only for a claude.ai login, so a gateway token, an `apiKeyHelper` or an API key gets the built-in list; under an organization's managed MCP config, where Claude Code refuses `--strict-mcp-config`, every pin stays `unverified`. On Codex the binary is the nearest `codex` ancestor process, the target of the `apply_patch` alias, `CODEX_CLI_PATH` when the environment carries it, `codex` on PATH or a CLI that an installed app bundles, of `CODEX_VERSION` when that is set, and no Codex config file is read; the list is the account catalog Codex caches in `models_cache.json` when the cache comes from that binary's version and is at most 24 hours old, otherwise the output of `codex debug models`, which counts as the account's only outside the command sandbox and when it differs from `codex debug models --bundled`. This replaces the earlier check against `codex debug models` from PATH, which silently printed the bundled catalog when it could not fetch the account's. `generate_claude_project.py apply` and `generate_codex_project.py apply` render the roles of an `unavailable` model on the session's model at their own effort, Claude Code's as `model: inherit` and Codex's without `model`, print a warning that names the model, its tiers and its roles, and record the verdict in the managed files as `# Model unavailable: <model>`, so `check` and `inspect` render the same and every apply judges the model again; a rendered Claude role keeps the stamp of its resolved settings, so the session start check finds it current. An `unverified` model keeps its pin with a note, and a project model outside the catalog keeps the effort the project set, with a warning when the list does not name that effort for it. Both generators report `model_check`, with the list's source, view and each model's verdict, and `model_fallbacks`. On Codex a run-time record of `--inherit-model`, `# Model fallback: <model>`, stays until `--restore-model <model>` or `--execution-profile auto`, and the run-time warning comes from the coordinator rule, because Codex has no hook event for a failed role. `python3 <package-scripts>/host_models.py [MODEL ...]` prints the listing with each model's verdict and effort levels.
